# Uppāda Saṁyutta (SN 26)

**ID:** SN 26

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppāda Saṁyutta* (SN 26), translated as "Linked Discourses on Arising" or "Connected Discourses on Arising," is the twenty-sixth chapter of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [Bodhi 2003]. Together with the *Okkanta Saṁyutta* (SN 25) and *Kilesa Saṁyutta* (SN 27), it forms a closely related triad of sections constructed upon a shared structural foundation [Bodhi 2003]. This foundation systematically classifies experience according to a tenfold doctrinal template (beginning with the six internal sense bases and proceeding through external sense bases, consciousness, and elements) [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. Set at Sāvatthī, the suttas declare that the arising (*uppāda*), continuation, production, and manifestation of these factors (such as the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind) constitute the arising of suffering (*dukkha*), the persistence of disease, and the manifestation of aging-and-death [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. Bhikkhu Bodhi notes that the ninth sutta corresponds closely to SN 14.36, but expands the elements to include space and consciousness [Bodhi 2003]. Modern scholars of Sarvāstivāda scholasticism note that the tenfold categories across the *Okkanta*, *Uppāda*, and *Kilesa Saṁyuttas* were cited by Yamada Ryūjō as early scriptural precedents for the Abhidharma classification of mental factors into tenfold schemes [Willemen, Dessein, and Cox 1998].
